title: Becoming all things; one prize for the one body; gift and remaining worthy
english: —the lawless. At the same time he keeps his own exactness. “I became to the Jews as a Jew”: he did not say here, “not being a Jew.” For he was a Jew in secret, no longer in the open. And again: “to those under law as under law, though not myself under law”—here he had to put “not myself under law,” for [[Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law >> Bible:Galatians 3:13]], becoming a curse for us; as if he said, “not being a Samaritan.” “To the lawless as lawless, not being lawless toward God.” Someone will suppose I have become an apostate from the law and lawless toward God; I say that even if I do not keep the law according to the letter, I am not lawless toward God but under Christ’s law, keeping the polity according to the gospel, that I may win the lawless.

“I became to the weak as weak”: he did not say here “not myself being weak.” For it would have been boastful and arrogant, and not according to the apostle, to say “not myself being weak,” when he had heard from the Lord that [[my power is perfected in weakness >> Bible:2 Corinthians 12:9]] and for that reason boasts in weaknesses. How then was he weak to the weak? When he permits those who burn to marry; when he sympathizes with women who have lost husbands; when he says, [[because of porneias let each man have his own wife and each woman her own husband >> Bible:1 Corinthians 7:2]], and the rest. In these he became weak to the weak, that he might win the weak. Then after this he says, “I have become all things to all, that I may save all or some.” Whichever person you take, he is one of the five: either Jew, or under law, or lawless, or weak, or “all.” The perfect is all; so to all—that is, to the perfect—I have become perfect, that I may win all. For he says, [[we speak wisdom among the perfect >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:6]], and what follows. This one can say, “I am a debtor both to Greeks and barbarians, both to wise and to unwise.”

[Origen:] Only the perfect can utter the perfect apostle’s word in the Lord: “I do all things for the sake of the gospel.” The one who sins cannot say this. If the one who does all for the gospel is a partner of the gospel, the one who commits porneia is a partner of the porneia of the spirit—and likewise with the other passions. Each becomes partner of that with which he shared. But someone among the hearers will say, “My life is mixed: I do not do all for the gospel, nor all for sin and pleasure.” To this we will say: God has these judgments; according to his many and varied judgments he repays.

44 on [[1 Corinthians 9:24 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 9:24]]: “Do you not know that those who run in a stadium all run, but one receives the prize? So run that you may obtain.” [Origen:] Then do we all run and one receives the prize, and the rest perish? For he said one receives the prize while many run. All who are being saved are one and one body; for if we all share one bread and the same bread, we are all Christ’s body. So all the saved are the one who receives the prize. In the stadium, then, all run who order their life by a doctrine—those from the heresies who live by a doctrine, and perhaps Jews, and those who live by Greek doctrines while philosophizing. These are all who run in the stadium; the church also runs; but one receives the prize—the one man of whom the apostle says, [[until we all attain to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ >> Bible:Ephesians 4:13]]. Yet every judgment of God must be found concerning all who run in the stadium, so that one may take first place and then each according to his worth.

45 on [[1 Corinthians 10:5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:5]]: “But with most of them God was not well pleased, for they were struck down in the wilderness.” [Origen:] The apostle wants to show us that it is not merely obtaining a gift of God that saves the one who obtained it, but that after obtaining the gift one must remain, having become worthy of it. For also—

title: Israel’s gift unused; types against craving evil; testing spirits; lesser gifts
english: —the sons of Israel, though benefited so greatly, were not saved when they proved unworthy of God’s benefaction. For [[God was not well pleased with most of them >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:5]]; they were struck down in the wilderness. And since the sinners were more and the righteous fewer, for that reason God was not well pleased with the many sinners rather than with the few righteous.

46 on [[1 Corinthians 10:6 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:6]]: “These things became types for us, so that we should not be desirers of evils, as they also desired.” [Origen:] He says these things have become types for us, so that we should not be desirers of evils as they desired. Those things were written typologically with a view to us, so that when we read the sins for which they suffered these things, we may keep ourselves from falling into the same desires as theirs.

47 on [[1 Corinthians 12:3 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:3]]: “Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says ‘Jesus is anathema,’ and no one can say ‘Jesus is Lord’ except in the Holy Spirit.” [Origen:] There are many differences among spirits, which no one will know accurately unless he has the gift of discernment of spirits. And so that we may not too rashly either reject the spirits in those who speak or approve them, John says in the letter, [[Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits whether they are of God; every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in flesh is of God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not of God >> Bible:1 John 4:1-3]]. He also teaches us that when we hear people speaking we should neither assent at random nor rashly deny that what is said is from a divine spirit, but that each hearer, knowing he risks in the very act of approving or rejecting, should attend carefully neither to trust the false nor to distrust the true.

About this the apostle also adds next: [[If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that what I write is of God; but if anyone is ignorant, he is ignored >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:37-38]]. So not only is the one who ignores the apostle’s things ignored by God, but if someone ignores while speaking by a divine spirit—and were to say that he does not speak by a divine spirit—he is ignored by God. Through these things the apostle seems to teach that there is no human who does not have another spirit in him besides the spirit of the human that is in him. Whether he is alien to the faith or belonging to it, he has a spirit belonging to him from God.

How do we who hear the divine word need to learn that no one speaking in God’s Spirit says “Jesus is anathema”? Let us see: some can be ambiguous to those who do not know the facts accurately—whether they speak by God’s Spirit or not—while they anathematize Jesus. If ever you see a Jew expounding the divine Scriptures and not contemptibly, to the many, prophetic words, you might perhaps be in doubt whether God’s Spirit is also in that one. So that you may not be pulled about over such a person—whether a holy spirit is in him or not—Paul teaches that since every Jew says Jesus is anathema, and no one speaking in God’s Spirit says Jesus is anathema, the one who claims to know the law and the prophets while anathematizing Jesus does not have God’s Spirit. There is a heresy that does not receive the one who approaches unless he anathematize Jesus. And that heresy is worthy of the name it loved; for it is the heresy of the so-called Ophites, who say unlawful things in praise of the serpent, which is cursed by God.

48 on [[1 Corinthians 12:8–10 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:8-10]] and [[12:27–28 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:27-28]]: gifts of wisdom, knowledge, faith, healings, powers, prophecy, discernments, tongues, interpretation; and God set in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then gifts of healings, helps, governances, kinds of tongues. title: Two senses of prophecy; hyperbole and love above gifts
english: —prophecy that has surpassed and a prophecy that has gone up. He will call the more catholic sort, imitating the prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah, second rank after the apostleship; but this last-ranked sort after the gifts already named is such as: [[if you prophesy, and an unbeliever or ungifted person comes in, he is convicted by all, examined by all, the secrets of his heart become plain, and so falling on his face he will worship God and announce that God is truly among you >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:24-25]]. For this is not far from the working of powers and the gift of healings that happen for the amazement of those who see, so that the one prophesying may say, “You have this in your heart; from this sin you have come to the church.” This prophecy can also be later in rank than the former ones, while that more divine and greater one is second, of which he says, [[God set in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:28]].

To establish that two things are signified from the name “prophecy,” I set out beforehand what I said. See whether I can still show the saying more clearly: God set in the church first apostles—but not all are apostles; for if all were apostles, to whom would they minister the apostleship? Second, prophets—not all are prophets; yet according to the other prophecy, “if you all prophesy, and an unbeliever or ungifted person comes in,” it is spoken not as of an impossibility but as of a possibility that all prophesy in that way. So there are two significations from the name “prophecy.” Therefore here too the apostle’s order is kept that says first apostles, second prophets, and the rest. So much concerning the order, since the phrase “to another prophecy,” ranked last in another wording, seemed to press us.

49 on [[1 Corinthians 13:1–2 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:1-2]]: “And I show you a still more excellent way. If I speak with the tongues of humans and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a sounding bronze or a clanging cymbal. And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.” [Origen:] We ask here whether someone in this life can both have prophecy and know all the mysteries without love, and altogether whether it is given to anyone to know all mysteries; for Paul says, [[If anyone thinks he has come to know something, he does not yet know as he ought to know >> Bible:1 Corinthians 8:2]]; and again, [[we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, the partial will be done away >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:9-10]]. Saying these things about himself and the apostles like him shows that it is not possible to know all mysteries and all knowledge. How then does he speak as if it were possible to know all knowledge and understand all mysteries?

If we look at the preface of the words, in which he says, “And I show you a still more excellent way,” and understand what “excellence” (hyperbole) is, all this will be clarified. Hyperbole, then, as even the Greeks defined it, is speech that for the sake of emphasis overshoots the truth; and they use the example that some are said to be whiter than snow—not that anything can be whiter than snow, but it is said by hyperbole. And again: some horses run like wind—not that such a thing is possible, but for emphasis, so that the horses’ speed may be shown, such a thing is said of them. And in the Scripture of the Psalms it is said of the sea, [[their waves go up to the heavens and go down to the abysses >> Bible:Psalm 107:26]]—which is impossible, but said for emphasis. And in the law you will find the manner of hyperbole written where it is written, [[We saw cities great and walled up to heaven >> Bible:Deuteronomy 1:28]]. How can this be? Yet it is said hyperbolically, the speech not altogether presenting the thing signified itself but showing the greatness of the waves or the lowliness, and the greatness of the walls, or something near these.

So also here the apostle takes a hypothesis in order that the nature of gifts and the nature of love may be examined—not that it is possible for a gift, and so great a gift, to exist without love; or that it is possible in this life for someone to know all knowledge without love, or to have such faith as to move mountains; but wanting to show that if love were set in a balance—the word being spoken by hypothesis. He says, then, that one must especially zealously pursue love. Do angels—

title: Angel dialects; knowledge vs mysteries; giving and martyrdom without love; love’s praises
english: —conversing with one another—do they converse in these same tongues humans use, so that some angels would happen to be Greek, some Hebrew, others Egyptian? Or is it absurd to say this about the upper angelic ranks? Then perhaps, just as there are many dialects among humans, so also among angels? And if God grants us to be ranked from human nature into the angelic—my Lord Jesus Christ promising that [[they will be as angels and sons of God, being sons of the resurrection >> Bible:Luke 20:36]]—will we no longer use a human dialect but the angelic dialect? And just as children’s dialect differs from that of those whose voice is clear, so every human dialect is somehow a children’s dialect, while the angelic is somehow that of perfect and clear-voiced men? And perhaps there too, according to the analogy of their station, there are dialects. “If then I speak with the tongues of humans and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a sounding bronze or a clanging cymbal.” Just as sounding bronze gives an indistinct voice, and the clanging cymbal nothing clear, in the same way, without love, a tongue—even of angels among humans by hypothesis—is unclear; for nothing makes human or angelic speech clear and plain as love does; when love is absent, what is spoken is nothing.

What is the difference between knowledge and knowing the mysteries? For the apostle speaks about two things. I hold, then, that knowing about the open things is knowledge, more generic than the mysteries; for within a part of knowledge lies the science of the mysteries. But knowing about the more unspeakable and more divine things is knowing the mystery—so that there is a generic account of knowledge, yet not every grasp of knowledge is grasp of mysteries, about which it is said, [[But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom which God predestined before the ages for our glory >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:7]]. When I know these things, then I have the knowledge of the mysteries. “And if I have all faith so as to move mountains”: it is written in the gospel, [[If you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you >> Bible:Matthew 17:20]]. For the one who has faith as a mustard seed has the whole of faith.

50 on [[1 Corinthians 13:3 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:3]]: “And if I give away all my possessions as food, and if I hand over my body that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.” [Origen:] “If I feed people with all my goods” not because of love; “if I hand over my body that I may boast”—as if it were possible to give away goods not for love but for empty glory, and as if it were possible also to bear witness for the sake of boasting and the glory with which martyrs are glorified in the churches.

51 on [[1 Corinthians 13:4–5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:4-5]]: “Love is patient, is kind; love does not envy; love does not brag, is not puffed up, does not behave indecently, does not seek its own.” [Origen:] He goes through the praises of the love that surpasses the gifts. For he had to teach both what love is and how the one who has love is. “Love is patient”: if you have patience that is a fruit of the Spirit, you have it because of love. “Is kind”: what is opposite to kindness? Wickedness. If you act wickedly against anyone, you do not have love. If you are kind and sweet toward all humans, you have love. “Love does not envy”: if there is envy in you like Cain’s toward Abel or like Joseph’s brothers toward Joseph, you do not have love. Loving and envying are fighting things. “Love does not brag”: when someone is rash, professing to know about a craft or a science or knowledge, that one is the braggart because he does not have love. “Does not behave indecently”: no one who has love does anything indecent; so if ever a brother and sister claiming to love one another according to God fall through weakness under the pretext of love, let us tell them they do not have love; for love does not behave indecently. “Does not seek its own”: no one who has love seeks his own things; for example a mother loving her son, or a father, does not seek his own as he seeks the son’s; for having love is not self-loving. title: Love unto death; tongues cease; part and perfect; building gifts; clear sound
english: of death, even death on a cross. Come also to the saints; see Moses’ love: [[If you forgive them their sin, forgive; if not, blot me out of your book which you have written >> Bible:Exodus 32:32]]. And the apostle also says, [[just as I also please all in all things, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, that they may be saved >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:33]], and [[I could wish to be anathema from Christ for my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh >> Bible:Romans 9:3]]. He prays to be anathema from Christ for the salvation of others.
52 on [[1 Corinthians 13:8 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:8]]: “Whether tongues, they will cease.” [Origen:] Tongues will cease when I converse with mind to the one with whom I wish to speak.

53 on [[1 Corinthians 13:9–12 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:9-12]]: “For we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, then the partial will be done away. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, thought as a child, reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I did away with the things of the child. For now we see through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face.” [Origen:] The one who seems to advance here advances as among children; but when the perfect comes and we attain to a perfect man, then we will contain the things of men—knowledge and prophecy and the vision of God which the blessed will see because of purity of heart.

54 on [[1 Corinthians 14:5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:5]]: “For the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive building.” [Origen:] The one who has the building gift is greater than the one who does not, inasmuch as the one with the building gift is more useful to the common good; but if the one speaking in tongues also has interpretation for building the church, the prophet is no longer greater. For sometimes he speaks high things, speaking to himself and to God, so that the church cannot hear.

55 on [[1 Corinthians 14:6 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:6]]: “But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you unless I speak to you either in revelation or in prophecy or in knowledge or in teaching?” [Origen:] Prophecy is knowledge that signifies the unseen through speech—knowledge of the world’s constitution and of the working of elements and times. Teaching is the instructional word distributed to the many. Revelation is when the mind goes outside earthly things and puts away every fleshly practice by God’s power; the one who obtains this has come into revelation. Perhaps also knowledge about future things can be called revelation; and one who has understood each term’s proper sense may use the names more loosely.

56 on [[1 Corinthians 14:7–9a >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:7-9]]: lifeless flute or lyre without distinction of notes; trumpet without clear call; tongues without clear speech. [Origen:] He wants to shame those who speak in a tongue into silence in church if there is no interpreter. Lifeless flute and lyre that give no distinction of musical notes are not known by what rhythm they played; the soldier does not arm for war unless the trumpet utters the voice that rouses to war; and those who speak in a tongue and do not interpret ought not to speak, as giving no distinction to the words for understanding. He called the doctrines of contemplation flute and lyre as showing nothing ethical, and those who urge toward virtue a trumpet. Hence one may say that the unclear parts of Scripture—such as the sacrifices in Leviticus and the tent in Exodus—should not be read unless someone clarifies their mind by exposition.

57 on [[1 Corinthians 14:9b >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:9]]: “For you will be speaking into the air.” [Origen:] The one who speaks in a tongue speaks in God; even if humans do not understand, still the powers about the air hear.
58 on [[1 Corinthians 14:10 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:10]]: “There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is voiceless.”

title: Voiceless bodies; barbarian speech; abound for building; pray with mind; five words
english: [Origen:] So even the lifeless give voice, some with this distinction of notes, some without it; for every body has a property of voice when it strikes another body.

59 on [[1 Corinthians 14:11 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:11]]: “If then I do not know the force of the voice, I will be a barbarian to the speaker and the speaker a barbarian in me.” [Origen:] Everyone who speaks to someone what that one does not understand seems a barbarian to the hearer, and that one to him.

60 on [[1 Corinthians 14:12 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:12]]: “So also you, since you are zealots for spirits, seek to abound toward the building of the church.” [Origen:] Abounding happens by the superiority of gifts from seeking what builds the church, inasmuch as the one who does not seek the common good does not abound in the gifts. For likely the working of the gift is idle when it does not shine before humans. Therefore if we want the gifts to grow, we will give ourselves over to the benefit of the many.

61 on [[1 Corinthians 14:13–14 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:13-14]]: “Therefore let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret. For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.” [Origen:] If the tongue speaker does not have the gift of interpreting, even if others do not understand, he himself understands what is cast into him from the spirit so that he is moved to speak. But when what is spoken is understood by others, then that seems to be fruit of the speaker toward those who understand.

62 on [[1 Corinthians 14:15–17 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:15-17]]: pray and sing with spirit and mind; otherwise the ungifted cannot say Amen and is not built. [Origen:] Through these too we are taught to seek the common good of the church.

63 on [[1 Corinthians 14:18–19 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:18-19]]: “I thank my God, speaking in tongues more than you all; but in church I want to speak five words with my mind, that I may also catechize others, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.” [Origen:] Even speaking the sense words spiritually is seeking the common good of the five senses; and the word of catechesis through the five senses is set for the hearers in church, as they too are catechized by the five words. For those who do not know the clarity of what is said, but attend only to the bare sound of the Scriptures, are called catechumens; but those who hear the distinction of the notes from Scripture are not catechumens but faithful.

64 on [[1 Corinthians 14:20 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:20]]: “Brothers, do not be children in your minds, but be infants in evil, and in your minds become perfect.” [Origen:] Since what he commands is possible, it is possible for us to become perfect in our minds. This nearly interprets, [[Unless you turn and become as the children >> Bible:Matthew 18:3]]; for the one who is an infant in evil, having turned, becomes as a child.

65 on [[1 Corinthians 14:21 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:21]]: “In the law it is written, ‘In other tongues and with other lips I will speak to this people, and not even so will they hear me, says the Lord.’” [Origen:] He also called the prophetic word “law”; and we found these words in Aquila and the other editions, not indeed in the Seventy.

66 on [[1 Corinthians 14:24–25 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:24-25]]: if all prophesy, the unbeliever is convicted, heart secrets laid bare, and he falls and worships, announcing God is truly among you. [Origen:] Since the prophetic gift makes known the secrets of the unbeliever’s and ungifted person’s heart when he draws near them, clearly when the perfect comes they will know perfectly every ungifted and unbeliever’s secrets—and likely then also the holy person’s secrets become plain to the prophets, perhaps the greater knowing the lesser’s. And the one benefited is cautious to look into God’s face; therefore imagining God he falls on his face, giving him the superiority and glory, and so worships God. Convicting and examining the heart’s secrets—that is, making them plain—marks that God is in the spirit of such people. And if the other gifts too are signs that God truly is, in what must one seek?

67 on [[1 Corinthians 14:26–27 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:26-27]]: when you come together each has a psalm, teaching, tongue, revelation, interpretation; let all be for building; if anyone speaks in a tongue, by two or at most three, and in turn, and let one—

title: Interpret in turn; discern spirits; prophets silent; women silent; spiritual examiner
english: interpret. [Origen:] When we come together, all who have gifts and are able to teach must be allowed to speak.

68 on [[1 Corinthians 14:29 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:29]]: “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern.” [Origen:] By “others” he means those who have the gift of clarifying the prophets’ spiritual words, if indeed the prophesying ones themselves did not have the gift of discernment; for in what they lack this, they may well have been deceived by some wicked spirit transforming itself into an angel of light, as if they had obtained prophetic rank.

69 on [[1 Corinthians 14:30–31 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:30-31]]: “If a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first be silent. For you can all prophesy one by one.” [Origen:] Therefore the prophets were not beside themselves; for in them was the power to be silent and to hold back the spirit upon them.

70 on [[1 Corinthians 14:32 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:32]]: “And spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.” [Origen:] For this reason the subjection shows willingly in silence; that the spirits are subject to the prophets, but it is the prophets’ souls that prophesy.

71 on [[1 Corinthians 14:34–35 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:34-35]]: “Let your women be silent in the churches; for it is not permitted them to speak, but to be subject, as also the law says. If they wish to learn something, let them ask their own husbands at home.” [Origen:] Since from the beginning the men had authority to speak and benefit the hearers, and the women asked about what they were unsure of. And by “law” he means what is said in Genesis, [[Your turning shall be to your husband >> Bible:Genesis 3:16]].

72 on [[1 Corinthians 14:37–38 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:37-38]]: “If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that what I write to you are the Lord’s commandments; but if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.” [Origen:] Spiritual is the one able to test every word and every mind, and through great depth of mind hard to diagnose so as not to be examined. It is not for just anyone to know that what Paul writes is the Lord’s, but for a prophet or spiritual; therefore the one who does not know it is the Lord’s is neither prophet nor spiritual. Believing is one thing and knowing another; therefore the one ignorant that it is the Lord’s is ignorant, not yet having arrived at truly being God’s; for the one known is somehow mixed into the one who knows him.

73 on [[1 Corinthians 14:31 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:31]]: “For you can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all be encouraged.” [Origen:] There is danger for those who read to declare simply, and likewise for those who hear. Hear Paul saying, [[If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual among you, let him acknowledge that what I write is of God >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:37]], as if not everyone knows the things of God unless he is prophet or spiritual. And the apostle sketched the spiritual when he said, [[The spiritual examines all things, yet he himself is examined by no one >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:15]]. Who is the one discerning all things but the one able to scrutinize and judge every word? And he is examined by no one, because the depth of his thoughts is not grasped. For the spiritual has the mind of the Lord. Just as a child cannot examine a man’s mind and scrutinize his thoughts—for the small child does not even follow a man’s thoughts at the start—so neither can the soulish know which things are God’s and which are not; this work belongs only to the spiritual.

I often asked myself why, when there were God’s prophets and false prophets, the false prophets were in favor with their kings more than the prophets; and the false prophets’ books were not written or preserved among the people, while the books of the prophets who were condemned, hated, and suffered what we know came into the open and are honored. What was the beginning of this? Taking cues from the apostle I say: there was a gift among the people, as of prophesying, so also of discerning prophets. “For you can all prophesy one by one”: there was then abundance of speakers and of those permitted to speak. For this reason the apostle allowed all to speak in church; he almost allowed even the women to speak, if he had not said what follows.

74 on [[1 Corinthians 14:34–35 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:34-35]] again: women silent in churches; ask husbands at home; shameful for women to speak in church. [Origen:] As if all speak and can speak when a revelation comes to them, he says women are to be silent in the churches. The women’s disciples—those discipled by Priscilla and Maximilla—were not of this commandment, not of Christ the—

title: Prophetesses not in assembly; own men; Corinth disorder; stand in the gospel
english: husband of the bride. But still let us be fair and meet even their plausible points. They say Philip the evangelist had four daughters and they prophesied. If they prophesied, what is absurd, as those people say, if our women also prophesy as prophetesses? We will solve this. First by saying: our women prophesied—show the signs of prophecy in them. Second: even if Philip’s daughters prophesied, they did not speak in the churches; for we do not have this in the Acts of the Apostles. Nor in the old: Deborah is attested a prophetess, and Miriam sister of Aaron took the tambourine and led the women. But you would not find that Deborah harangued the people like Jeremiah and Isaiah; you would not find that Huldah, being a prophetess, spoke to the people but to one who came to her. And in the gospel Anna is recorded a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel of Asher’s tribe; but she did not speak in church. So even if a woman is granted to be a prophetess from a prophetic sign, she is still not permitted to speak in church. When Miriam the prophetess spoke she was leader of certain women; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church, and [[I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man >> Bible:1 Timothy 2:12]].

I will also show this from elsewhere, even if that was said more securely about the woman not becoming leader by the man’s word: [[an older woman in a deportment sacred, a good teacher, that she may train the young women >> Bible:Titus 2:3-4]]—not simply that they teach. For let women also be good teachers, not so that men sit and hear women as if men able to ambassad God’s word were lacking. “If they wish to learn something, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for women to speak in church.” It seems to me “their own husbands” does not refer only to married men; for virgins would either speak in church or have no teachers, and widows likewise; but perhaps “own men” such as brother and household member and son? Once for all let a woman inquire of her own man according to the generic name “man” over against “woman”; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church, whatever she may say, even if she says wonders, even if holy things, only because it comes from a woman’s mouth. “Woman in church” is clearly said under the shameful for accusation of the whole church.

[[1 Corinthians 14:36 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:36]]: “Or did the word of God go out from you, or did it come to you alone?” As if this disorder was in Corinth along with the other sins. So he says God sent his word into the world. Did the truth and the church rule then come only to you Corinthians?

75 on [[1 Corinthians 14:37–38 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:37-38]]: acknowledge what I write are the Lord’s commands; if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant. [Origen:] So that we may know the things of God, let us ask the Giver of gifts to give us a prophetic gift and make us spiritual from the ruling spirit; and so be ready to judge which things are God’s and which are not. For the one deprived of this grace cannot understand; hence he added, “If anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.”

76 on [[1 Corinthians 15:1–2 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:1-2]]: “I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I gospelled to you, which also you received, in which also you stand, through which also you are saved, by what word I gospelled to you, if you hold it fast—unless you believed in vain.” [Origen:] He calls gospel what he gospels, for this he also handed on; and this one stands in the gospel who has his soul mounted on it as on a boat, through which he is also saved. And he says the one who does not hold the gospel’s word has believed in vain—having heard irrationally and by chance and not by examination. [Origen:] Jews have not stood in the gospel, not receiving Jesus; those from the heresies stand badly, not understanding the gospel but taking it in their own way; those who sin have not stood, not living according to the gospel. Who then have stood in the gospel but those who received it and accepted it and live according to it? And if “by what word I gospelled to you, if you hold fast” is understood, and the following “unless you believed in vain” is understood reasonably with these, we will know that it is impossible for the one who believed in vain thus—

title: Vain belief; Cephas and the Twelve; grace; resurrection of the flesh
english: —believed a falsehood; but to have believed what is true is not yet a work; belief is in judgment. Those who believe before the time and fall away in a time of trial believe in vain; and yet they have not believed false things but the true—yet because they have not believed firmly, for that reason they fall away in a time of trial. For one who believes well will not fall.

77 on [[1 Corinthians 15:5 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:5]]: “And that he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.” [Origen:] He says the Lord appeared to the Twelve after the resurrection; for it is likely that Matthias also was present, who was set as apostle in Judas’s place.

78 on [[1 Corinthians 15:9 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:9]]: “For I am the least of the apostles, who am not fit to be called apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.” [Origen:] Conscious of the sins from which he was freed, he says, “I am not fit to be called apostle.”

79 on [[1 Corinthians 15:10 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:10]]: “But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not empty, but I labored more abundantly than they all—yet not I, but the grace of God that is with me.” [Origen:] Having said that his grace toward me was not empty, he taught that those who live unworthily of the grace received it empty. It is not that grace labors, but it must be understood thus: “I did not do these things, but the grace that is with me.”

80 on [[1 Corinthians 15:11 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:11]]: “Whether then I or they, so we preach and so you believed.” [Origen:] All the apostles having been fully persuaded about Christ’s resurrection from the dead, the proof is firm; therefore we say the same things; for you also believed thus.

81 on [[1 Corinthians 15:12–13 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:12-13]]: if Christ is preached raised, how do some say there is no resurrection of the dead? [Origen:] Christ’s resurrection with the flesh he had is clear from the text before us. But some, or rather the heterodox, want to allegorize humans’ resurrection; let them allegorize the Savior’s too, badly rejecting the wording. [[He means Manicheans who say that the one freed from sins thus rose from the dead.]]

82 on [[1 Corinthians 15:14 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:14]]: “If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is empty, and your faith is empty.” [Origen:] Since neither the preaching nor the faith is empty, it is clear Christ has been raised. We noted these things to show that even if Paul knew dialectical arguments, he used them naturally; for from nature and custom the dialectical art was embodied by those who philosophize.

83 on [[1 Corinthians 15:15–16 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:15-16]]: false witnesses of God if the dead are not raised. [Origen:] If the one who says Christ rose bears false witness against God, then also everyone who says there is a resurrection of the dead; but if Christ rose as firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, it is clear the dead are raised.

84 on [[1 Corinthians 15:20–23 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:20-23]]: Christ raised as firstfruits; through a human death and resurrection; in Adam all die, in Christ all made alive; each in his own order. [Origen:] Since those from the heresies who say the church faith and sneer at it as faith of fools reject in deed, if not in word, that resurrection happens as the church believes—see how one must meet them from this apostolic wording and from countless others. Did Christ rise from the dead, or not? But every heresy has agreed about this. If Christ rose from the dead, and he is firstborn from the dead, and no one is firstborn of another kind, his resurrection must be of the same kind as the resurrection of those who rise. For example: Reuben is firstborn, being a son of Jacob—

title: Same-genus rising; seed and stalk; sown corruptible, raised spiritual
english: —of brothers of the same kind; for Reuben is not of another nature and Simeon or Levi and the rest of another. And with the other firstborns it is the same. If then Jesus also is firstborn from the dead, the resurrection of those who rise must be of the same kind. And if he wore a body, and his resurrection was with a body so that he even ate, as is written in the Gospel according to John, while those who rise among believers in Christ rise otherwise, as those from the heresies think, they cannot show how Jesus is firstborn from the dead. For if we have become conformed to the death of Christ, we shall also be conformed to his resurrection; and how does Paul teach saying, [[who will transform the body of our humiliation conformed to the body of Christ’s glory >> Bible:Philippians 3:21]]?

Some shamelessly admit that Christ has been raised from the dead, yet say there is no resurrection of the dead. Therefore the apostle says, [[If Christ is preached that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:12]]. Even if someone does not say it with the mouth, but says in the heart “there is no resurrection of the dead,” he effectively rejects also Jesus Christ’s resurrection. For if the universal is false, clearly the one who rose from the dead is also contained in the universal. For if the dead are not raised, and Jesus also was among the dead, then Jesus has not been raised either; but if he has been raised, through him the resurrection of the dead is shown—unless we disbelieve the thing as impossible in itself, forgetting who promised. For what, among impossibles so to speak, is more impossible: that the body be made alive, or that heaven come to be from things that are not, or the sun, or the rest of the creatures?

Come also to the human’s very beginning; recall his beginning. A human seed is shown you. If someone said, “This seed will be a human; it will be formed; there will be bones from it, flesh, sinews, veins; he will walk; from this small, cheap seed a human raised on earth will use organs”—would we not call the one preaching this to us mindless, if we had not taken experience of it? So then let me dare also to show you the resurrection, and you will rather accept it, trusting God’s perfection. What that seed was toward this present body—now the present, the generic, the sowing, the organ of words and works according to righteousness—this body becomes toward that: [[Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it falls into the earth and dies and decays, from the decay of the wheat grain a hundredfold ear comes >> Bible:John 12:24]]. That your body is seed of what will rise, hear Paul saying: [[It is sown in corruption, raised in incorruption; sown in dishonor, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power; sown a soulish body, raised a spiritual body >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:42-44]]. You see how there, upon the seed, something cheap and of no account was sown, and a fair and beautiful human was raised; in the same way this dead thing is a grain of wheat to God as what is about to rise. Just as God had means from the wheat grain to make an ear—not outside the starting points in the small seed; for from that he raised the ear, and from each seed he raises what potentially exists in the seed—so from a human seed according to the beginning this human came to be. And if his body dies, it becomes seed of the one who will rise from the dead in glory in Christ Jesus.

And the apostle took unbelief in the resurrection from the dead as equal to not believing that we shall exist at all after departure. Therefore to those who do not believe there will be a resurrection of the dead he says, as if according to them there is no other life besides the present, [[If in this life only we have hoped in Christ, we are of all humans most pitiable >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:19]]. And in what follows also, as according to those who say there is no resurrection of the dead, nor life existing beyond this life, he says, [[Why are we also in danger every hour? I die daily >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:30-31]], and the rest. And the heresy of the Sadducees who reject the resurrection of the dead also shows that it follows for them that you do not even live after the present life. Therefore the Savior toward them takes from the law alone an example about there being a resurrection from the dead, saying the wording—

title: God of the living; firstfruits of all; daily dying; how the dead rise; all changed
english: About the resurrection of the dead, have you not read that God said at the bush, [[I am the God of Abraham and the God of Jacob? He is not God of the dead but of the living >> Bible:Matthew 22:31-32]]. “But now Christ has been raised from the dead; he became firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.” Firstfruits is firstfruits of many. As we saw in the law’s examples: firstfruits of wheat is offered by those who harvested wheat; and say of wine by those who gathered wine; and of oil from those who crushed olive; so if our Lord Jesus Christ is firstfruits of those fallen asleep, there must be many of whom he is firstfruits; and we ask whether he is firstfruits of all or of many? For Christ, it says, is firstfruits of those fallen asleep. If we did not have a wording from the start, we might even say—thinking it somehow ill-omened here to call him firstfruits of all—that he is firstfruits of the righteous fallen asleep only, not of the rest. But now the apostle himself also says, [[For since through a human came death, through a human also resurrection of the dead >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:21]]; how then does he say of some what he says of all? For as in Adam all die, so in Christ—he did not say “the righteous will be made alive” but [[all will be made alive >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:22]].

Then so that you not be disturbed and say, “Was so much toil poured out for me in vain, if Christ raised from the dead is firstfruits of all who have fallen asleep and in Christ all will be made alive?” he says, [[But each in his own order >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:23]]. So all died in Adam, and all will be made alive in Christ; yet even though all died in Adam, Abraham was no less righteous, Isaac was a patriarch, Jacob who fathered the twelve patriarchs was Israel; and so one will come also to the other righteous. I dare say that while the apostle said Christ Jesus is firstfruits of those fallen asleep, I would put beside that: this one is firstfruits unto life of those who will live, while Adam has become firstfruits of humans’ death; for in Adam all die, he having taken the firstfruits of death; but the Savior, wanting to take up the firstfruits of life, first took up the death of the dead, that having abolished death he might become firstfruits of those fallen asleep and of the living.

85 on [[1 Corinthians 15:31 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:31]]: “I die daily, by your boasting which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.” [Origen:] One must inquire whether he did not transgress the gospel command that says [[Do not swear at all >> Bible:Matthew 5:34]].
86 on [[1 Corinthians 15:32 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:32]]: “If according to man I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what is the profit to me?” [Origen:] There are also intelligible beasts.

87 on [[1 Corinthians 15:35–38 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:35-38]]: how are the dead raised, with what body; fool, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies; you sow bare grain; God gives each seed its own body. [Origen:] Then is the human seed useless to the Craftsman beside all those bodies, so that one hopes for a resurrection of the dead, if one may say so, in olive fashion and vine fashion and wheat fashion, and from the fig’s pip so great a fig rises, and you do not laugh at what you see by experience? And if someone tells you that from this small thing a fruit-bearing fig rises, having learned by experience you do not mock; but because the time has not yet come for what will rise from the human body according to the resurrection from the dead to spring up, you will not wait to see this too? Or do you not know that for all other seeds not every season is fit for seeds to spring? But a wheat grain rises at this time of year; the grape-stone at this hour of year; the olive pit in this month, not at every time. And do you want, for the human body, so that you may believe, the dead to rise yearly like the grape-stone, like the olive, and not see one paradoxical time that you may know the resurrection of the dead? What is the one time? At the consummation of the age, so that after the resurrection from the dead you may no longer be in the present evil age. For Jesus Christ suffered that he might deliver us from the present evil age; and we redeem the time because the days are evil. So God well stewarded this too with the rest.
88 on [[1 Corinthians 15:51 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 15:51]]: “Behold, I tell you a mystery: we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed.”

title: Living like Paul; Timothy and Apollos; watch, stand, act in love
english: [Origen:] Paul in the first letter to the Thessalonians calls all like himself living; for the God of the living is also God of Paul and of those like him.

89 on [[1 Corinthians 16:10–12 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 16:10-12]]: if Timothy comes, see that he be with you without fear, for he works the Lord’s work as I also do; let no one despise him; send him on in peace; about Apollos I urged him much to come, and it was not at all will that he come now; he will come when he has opportunity. [Origen:] At the letter’s start he said, [[I hear there are divisions among you; each of you says, ‘I am of Paul,’ ‘I am of Apollos’ >> Bible:1 Corinthians 1:11-12]]—this Apollos about whom he speaks while such faction and turmoil is in the Corinthians’ church. This admirable Apollos, being overseer of those at that time, fled as to a judge to the apostle. Paul was doing the work of the apostleship; it was not fitting for him, spending time then in Asia, to leave the things in Asia and come to Corinth; but instead of himself he chose Timothy and sent him to set right the things in Corinth, and necessarily sending him with the letter entrusted him to the church.

For when the saints visited benefiting the hearers, they did not arrive in weakness or in fear or in trembling; but when they came to the weaker, they visited in weakness and in fear and in trembling. Such were the Corinthians, so that not the great Paul visited them but the weak one, inasmuch as he said, [[I became to the weak as weak, that I might win the weak >> Bible:1 Corinthians 9:22]]. And for this reason he said, [[I also was with you in weakness >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:3]]; for this reason he also came in fear and much trembling, so that he might prevail with the hearers. Since then arriving in fear and trembling for the one about to benefit concerns the hearers, he now asks the Corinthians that Timothy be with them without fear; for he works the Lord’s work as I also do; what I would have done if I had visited you, Timothy does for you. So let no one despise him; for if you despise this one, you despise me also; for he works the Lord’s work as I also do. And send him on in peace, that he may come to me; now he comes to you to make peace. For he finds your faction in the church; but having agreed and been set right by what he says and taken up peace, send him on in your concord and peace, that he may come to me. For I await him with the brothers—which brothers? those of whom he said earlier, [[Whomever you approve by letters, these I will send >> Bible:1 Corinthians 16:3]]. So I await hearing him return, announcing to me your affairs.

About brother Apollos I urged him to come to you; and it was not at all will that he come now. He was a human, as is likely, holy, a friend of peace, and seeing faction and turmoil in the church under him, he did not claim this but yielded. Then the apostle asks him, having been patient, to return to his sojourning. And this one did not see Corinth at all, not disobeying the apostle; for he would not thus have recommended his seeming, if not subject; for he says, “It was not at all will that he come now”—that is, not without God’s will did he do the not coming to you; but he will come when he has opportunity. And when does he have opportunity? If you are at peace, if you do not despise Timothy.

90 on [[1 Corinthians 16:13–14 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 16:13-14]]: “Watch, stand in the faith, act like men, be strong. Let all your things be done in love.” [Origen:] For there is a sleep of soul and a watching; therefore the word, turning the soul from sleeping, says through Solomon, [[Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids, that you may be saved like a doe from snares and like a bird from a snare >> Bible:Proverbs 6:4-5]]. And the Savior says, [[Watch at every time and pray that you may be able to escape the trials that are about to come >> Bible:Luke 21:36]]. “Stand”: do not be shaken but become firm. The double-souled has not stood in the faith, or the one doubting about the things according to the faith. “Act like men”: he speaks as to soldiers; for [[put on the panoply of God, that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil >> Bible:Ephesians 6:11]]. “Be strong”: that is, take up the strength, that having been strengthened you may be able to say, [[I can do all things in Christ Jesus who strengthens me >> Bible:Philippians 4:13]]. “Let all your things be done in love”: for beginners, doing in fear; for the perfect, doing in love.
